title: Nephi’s Warning
summary: Nephi warns his brethren against supposing they are more righteous than the Gentiles and says all who do not keep God’s commandments will perish.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi addresses his beloved brethren.
Nephi says they should not suppose themselves more righteous than the Gentiles, and that those who do not keep God's commandments will likewise perish.
Nephi says they need not suppose the Gentiles are utterly destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi is visibly speaking to an audience of brethren.
unspecified_visual_details: The brethren's number, appearance, and setting are not specified.

narration.text: I, Nephi, would not suffer that ye should suppose that ye are more righteous than the Gentiles shall be.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Gentiles as present; they are mentioned in Nephi's address.

title: Repentance and the Covenant
summary: Nephi teaches that repentant Gentiles are the Lord’s covenant people and that unrepentant Jews will be cast off.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says repentant Gentiles are the Lord's covenant people; unrepentant Jews will be cast off.
The Lord covenants with those who repent and believe in his Son, the Holy One of Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi's teaching can be shown as off-screen speech over the supported setting.
unspecified_visual_details: No audience, divine appearance, or physical action is described in this verse.

narration.text: as many of the Gentiles as will repent are the covenant people of the Lord
the Lord covenanteth with none save it be with them that repent and believe in his Son

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The statements are teachings, not a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord or the Son as visibly present; no appearance is described.

title: Words Carried to the Remnant
summary: Nephi prophesies that after the book comes forth to the Gentiles and is sealed again to the Lord, many will believe its words and carry them to the remnant of Nephi’s seed.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi prophesies that after the book comes forth, is written unto the Gentiles, and is sealed up again unto the Lord, many will believe its words and carry them to the remnant of Nephi's seed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi can be shown speaking; the future events need not be staged as present action.
unspecified_visual_details: The book's appearance, the carriers' identities, and the place are not specified.

narration.text: there shall be many which shall believe the words which are written
they shall carry them forth unto the remnant of our seed

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The book's future circulation is prophesied, not narrated as a current event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the book's physical appearance or identify its future carriers.

title: The Remnant Learns Its Ancestry
summary: Nephi says the remnant of his seed will learn that his people came out from Jerusalem and that they are descendants of the Jews.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says the remnant of his seed will learn that his people came from Jerusalem and that the remnant are descendants of the Jews.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi can be shown speaking without depicting the future remnant as present.
unspecified_visual_details: The remnant's appearance, location, and the manner in which they learn this are unspecified.

narration.text: they are descendants of the Jews

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a future event reported in prophecy, not a present-time scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Jerusalem or the remnant as physically present without textual support.

title: The Gospel Declared
summary: Nephi prophesies that the gospel of Jesus Christ will be declared among the remnant, restoring knowledge of their fathers and of Jesus Christ.

explicit_facts.text: The gospel of Jesus Christ will be declared among the remnant, restoring their knowledge of their fathers and of Jesus Christ as known among their fathers.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown speaking over the unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The future declarers, audience, and circumstances are not specified.

narration.text: the gospel of Jesus Christ shall be declared among them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The declaration and restoration are future events in Nephi's prophecy.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the future declarers or depict Jesus Christ appearing.

title: Rejoicing and Enlightenment
summary: Nephi says the remnant will rejoice, recognize God’s blessing, and become a pure and delightsome people after many generations; he describes darkness falling from their eyes.

explicit_facts.text: The people will rejoice and know their change is a blessing from God.
Their scales of darkness will begin to fall from their eyes, and within many generations they will be a pure and delightsome people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The scales of darkness are figurative language for a change in understanding, not literal scales.
unspecified_visual_details: The people's appearance, setting, and manner of rejoicing are unspecified.

narration.text: they shall know that it is a blessing unto them from the hand of God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The scales of darkness are a figure of speech, not a literal supernatural visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show literal scales falling from eyes or invent a divine appearance.

title: Scattered Jews Gather
summary: Nephi prophesies that scattered Jews will begin to believe in Christ and gather upon the land; believers will become a delightsome people.

explicit_facts.text: Scattered Jews will begin to believe in Christ and gather upon the face of the land; those who believe will become a delightsome people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown speaking; no future gathering is required as a present scene.
unspecified_visual_details: The land, gathering place, participants' appearance, and timing are unspecified.

narration.text: the Jews which are scattered also shall begin to believe in Christ
they shall begin to gather in upon the face of the land

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The gathering is prophesied, not narrated as taking place during Nephi's speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage an unlocated future gathering as present action.

title: The Lord’s Work Among All Nations
summary: Nephi says the Lord God will begin his work among all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people to restore his people upon the earth.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God will commence his work among all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people to restore his people upon the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown delivering the prophecy.
unspecified_visual_details: No visible appearance of the Lord God, specific peoples, or location is described.

narration.text: to bring about the restoration of his people upon the earth

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a prophecy, not a narrated present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord God or invent a specific gathering scene.

title: Judgment with Righteousness
summary: Nephi prophesies that the Lord God will judge the poor with righteousness and reprove for the meek with equity; he uses figures of speech about the rod of his mouth and breath of his lips.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God will judge the poor with righteousness and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.
Nephi describes the Lord smiting with the rod of his mouth and slaying the wicked with the breath of his lips.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The rod of the mouth and breath of the lips are figurative expressions, not literal weapons or visible breath.
unspecified_visual_details: No visible appearance of the Lord God or specific judgment setting is described.

narration.text: with righteousness shall the Lord God judge the poor

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The rod and breath imagery should not be depicted as literal supernatural action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the Lord God appearing or add literal combat, weapons, or breath.

title: Division and the Wicked’s Destruction
summary: Nephi prophesies a great division among the people, the destruction of the wicked, and the sparing of the Lord’s people, even if destruction comes by fire.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God will cause a great division among the people, destroy the wicked, and spare his people, even if the wicked must be destroyed by fire.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The verse reports future events; Nephi may be shown speaking rather than staging them as current action.
unspecified_visual_details: The people, location, nature of the division, and any fire are not described.

narration.text: the Lord God shall cause a great division among the people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The destruction is prophetic; the verse does not describe a visible event occurring at this moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict fire or destruction as an occurring scene.

title: Righteousness and Faithfulness
summary: Nephi describes righteousness and faithfulness as the Lord’s girdle imagery.

explicit_facts.text: Righteousness is described as the girdle of the Lord's loins, and faithfulness as the girdle of his reins.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The girdles are figurative descriptions of righteousness and faithfulness.
unspecified_visual_details: The verse does not describe the Lord's appearance or clothing.

narration.text: righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Treat the girdle language as metaphor, not as an appearance description.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the Lord in garments or a visible form based on this metaphor.

title: Peace Among Animals
summary: Nephi prophesies that predator and prey animals will dwell and feed together, and that a little child will lead them; the lion will eat straw like the ox.

explicit_facts.text: The wolf will dwell with the lamb; the leopard with the kid, calf, young lion, and fatling; and a little child will lead them.
The cow and bear will feed, their young will lie down together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The animals and child can be illustrated as the peaceful future described in the prophecy.
unspecified_visual_details: The animals' colors, the child's identity and appearance, and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: then shall the wolf dwell with the lamb
the lion shall eat straw like the ox

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic descriptions of a future peaceful condition.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the child or add named characters.

title: Children and Serpents
summary: Nephi prophesies that a nursing child will play on an asp’s hole and a weaned child will put a hand on a cockatrice’s den.

explicit_facts.text: A sucking child will play on the hole of the asp, and a weaned child will put a hand on the cockatrice's den.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two children and serpent dens may be shown in the peaceful future described.
unspecified_visual_details: The children's identities, appearance, and location are unspecified.

narration.text: the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice’s den

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This verse belongs to the prophecy of peaceful conditions.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent identities or depict injury.

title: Nothing Hurts in the Holy Mountain
summary: Nephi prophesies that none will hurt or destroy in the Lord’s holy mountain, and that the earth will be full of the knowledge of the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: No one will hurt or destroy in the Lord's holy mountain, and the earth will be full of the knowledge of the Lord as waters cover the sea.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The waters covering the sea are a comparison expressing fullness, not a separate supernatural event.
unspecified_visual_details: The holy mountain's appearance and location are not specified.

narration.text: They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes a future condition and uses a simile about waters.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a specific mountain or depict knowledge as a visible substance.

title: All Things Made Known
summary: Nephi says the things of all nations and all things will be made known; secrets, works of darkness, and things sealed on earth will be revealed or loosed.

explicit_facts.text: The things of all nations and all things will be made known to the children of men.
Nothing secret will remain unrevealed, no work of darkness unmanifest in the light, and nothing sealed on earth will remain sealed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Light is figurative in the phrase about works of darkness being made manifest.
unspecified_visual_details: The things revealed, the manner of revelation, and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: all things shall be made known unto the children of men
There is nothing which is secret save it shall be revealed

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic teachings; do not depict abstract revelation as a specific event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent particular secrets, objects, or supernatural visual effects.

title: Nephi Ends His Sayings
summary: Nephi says all things revealed to humanity will be revealed in that day, Satan will no longer have power over human hearts for a long time, and he ends his sayings.

explicit_facts.text: All things revealed to humanity will be revealed at that day.
Satan will have power over human hearts no more for a long time.
Nephi says he makes an end of his sayings.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown concluding his address.
unspecified_visual_details: No appearance of Satan or divine figure is specified.

narration.text: And now, my beloved brethren, I make an end of my sayings.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The final statements are prophecy and conclusion, not a narrated visible appearance of Satan.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Satan or visualize power over hearts as a literal force.
